title: A scenario types the person's side of the conversation into coax
body:
`coax-fake-agent` plays one act of its scenario for each prompt it receives (`src/fake.rs`, `src/scenario.rs`), so a scenario can hold any number of turns. A new turn starts only when a person types a prompt into coax and presses Enter. ACP gives an agent no way to make its client send a prompt. `--prompt` sends the first one and nothing after it. A README recording of a back-and-forth conversation therefore needs someone to type each prompt by hand during the take.

## Proposal

- A scenario gains an optional top-level `input` list. Each step is `{"type": <text>, "per_char_ms": N}`, `{"key": <name>}` such as `"Enter"` or `"j"`, `{"delay_ms": N}`, or `{"wait": "idle"}`, which holds the input until the agent's turn has ended.
- A coax flag that exists only with the `fake-agent` feature reads a scenario's `input` and feeds each step into coax's event loop as the key events a person would type. `cargo install coax` gets no new flag.
- The `input` field is an addition to the scenario format, so older scenarios still load and the change is a patch.

## Rejected

- The fake agent sending `user_message_chunk` updates for the person's side. coax would draw the bubbles but treat the whole exchange as one agent turn. The working line would stay up between messages, and nothing would be typed into the prompt.
- `tmux send-keys` from outside coax. tmux sits between coax and the terminal and answers coax's colour queries itself, and the script would live outside the scenario.
